journal.title: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

result.abstractText:
Background

Evidence is limited regarding whether assigned protein targets modify responses to resistance training (RT) alone or to the same RT program plus cycling (concurrent training [CT]) in middle-aged and older women. This randomized 2 × 3 factorial trial examined bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA)-derived skeletal muscle mass (SMM; primary outcome), other body composition outcomes, muscular and functional performance, and cycle-derived estimated VO₂max.

Methods

In this randomized 2 × 3 factorial trial, 108 women aged 40-77 years were assigned to 12 weeks of supervised RT or CT (identical RT followed by cycling) and protein targets of 0.8, 1.6, or 2.2 g·kg-1·d-1. Baseline-adjusted ANCOVA tested training × protein interactions and marginal training and protein effects. Complete-case analyses included 83 participants.

Results

For SMM, no training-condition × protein-target interaction (p = 0.856), marginal protein-target effect (p = 0.726), or marginal training-condition effect (p = 0.273) was detected. CT had a lower baseline-adjusted week-12 BFP than RT (adjusted difference, -2.04 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.94 to -1.14; p < 0.001). RT had a higher baseline-adjusted week-12 leg-press estimated 1-RM than CT (CT - RT: -6.68 kg; 95% CI, -8.32 to -5.04; p < 0.001), whereas CT had a higher baseline-adjusted week-12 cycle-derived estimated VO₂max (adjusted difference, 4.53 mL·kg-1·min-1; 95% CI, 3.80 to 5.25; p < 0.001). No detectable marginal protein-target effects or training-condition × protein-target interactions were observed for the key secondary outcomes.

Conclusions

No detectable differences in SMM or key secondary outcomes were attributable to assigned protein target. Compared with RT, CT favored estimated aerobic fitness and BFP, whereas RT favored leg-press strength. Because CT included additional cycling and greater exercise exposure, these differences cannot be attributed solely to training modality. Null protein findings do not establish equivalence among doses.

journal.title: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders

result.abstractText:
Background

The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index serves as a surrogate marker for insulin resistance. Emerging evidence suggests that the TyG index may be associated with alterations in muscle mass, potentially impacting metabolic health. This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between the TyG index and skeletal muscle mass parameters across different demographic groups.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 3,781 participants (1,913 men and 1,868 women) aged 20 years and older (mean age 42.2 ± 12.6 years; range: 20-85 years) from the Tehran Lipid and Glucose Study (TLGS). Demographic, anthropometric, body composition (measured by bioelectrical impedance analysis), and metabolic data were collected. Appendicular skeletal muscle mass (ASM) and skeletal muscle mass index (SMI) were calculated, and low muscle mass was defined according to the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia criteria. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 27.0 to assess the association between the TyG index and ASM.

Results

Among 3,781 participants (mean age 42.2 ± 12.6 years), 6.37% exhibited low muscle mass. Higher TyG index quartiles were associated with greater skeletal muscle mass (SMM, ASMM, and SMMI; all P < 0.001), particularly in men. Sex-stratified analyses revealed stronger correlations in men (SMM: β = 1.30 kg per TyG unit, 95% CI 0.93-1.67) than women (β = 0.72 kg, 95% CI 0.47-0.97). Logistic regression showed lower odds of low muscle mass in higher TyG quartiles (men, Q4 OR: 0.34, 95% CI 0.15-0.76; women, Q4 OR: 0.73, 95% CI 0.40-1.31).

Conclusion

The TyG index shows a positive association with skeletal muscle mass, especially in men, indicating its potential as a biomarker associated with metabolic muscle status. These findings support its use for early risk assessment, though further research is needed to confirm its predictive value and guide clinical strategies.

result.abstractText:
Background

Age-related reductions in physical activity and unfavorable body composition changes promote metabolic dysfunction and cardiovascular risk elevation in older populations. Due to estrogen-related factors, differences in cardiovascular risks, and musculoskeletal conditions, exercise may be one of the most accessible and widely applicable lifestyle interventions for older women. A comprehensive and systematic search has not yet been carried out on the effects of exercise on cardiovascular risk and its related indicators in elderly women. This meta-analysis evaluates exercise effects on metabolic risk, cardiovascular health, and body composition in healthy elderly women.

Methods

Following PRISMA guidelines, we systematically searched PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, CNKI, VIP, Wanfang, and Sinomed (2014-2024) for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing supervised exercise with nonexercise controls. Data were analyzed with fixed- and random-effect models in Stata 17.0. The Cochrane RoB2 tool assessed bias risk, while the certainty of evidence was evaluated through the GRADE approach.

Results

Twenty-three RCTs (33 intervention arms, 23 controls) were included. Exercise significantly reduced triglycerides (TG) (-8.56 mg/dL, 95% CI: -16.72, -0.40), total cholesterol (TC)(-26.67 mg/dL, 95% CI: -34.92, -18.42), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) (-23.77 mg/dL, 95% CI: -34.48, -13.05), blood glucose (Glu) (-5.59 mg/dL, 95% CI: -10.12, -1.06), and C-reactive protein (CRP) (-0.86 mg/L, 95% CI: -1.37, -0.35). Cardiovascular improvements included increased VO2peak (+2.78 mL/kg/min, 95% CI: 1.87, 3.70) and reduced systolic blood pressure (SBP) (-8.35 mmHg) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) (-3.26 mmHg). Regarding body composition, relative body fat (RF, i.e. body fat percentage) decreased (-2.47%, 95% CI: -3.42, -1.53), but no significant changes were observed in body weight, trunk fat mass (TFM), waist circumference (WC), fat-free mass (FFM), or skeletal muscle mass (SMM). According to the GRADE framework, the evidence was of moderate certainty for reductions in TC, TG, RF, VO₂peak, and SBP; and low certainty for all other outcomes.

Conclusion

This meta-analysis provides evidence that appropriate exercise (aerobic, resistance, combined exercise) effectively reduces cardiovascular risk factors in elderly women via dual mechanisms of body composition remodeling and metabolic homeostasis enhancement, with particular efficacy in lipid regulation and blood pressure control.

result.abstractText:
Background

Menopause is accompanied by accelerated losses in muscle mass and strength and declining bone density. Whether creatine monohydrate benefits postmenopausal women are uncertain.

Methods

We systematically reviewed randomized, placebo-controlled trials examining creatine supplementation, with or without resistance training (RT), in postmenopausal women. MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, SPORTDiscus, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from 2000 to August 2025, supplemented by trial registries and reference-list screening. Eligible studies included postmenopausal women aged ≥40-45 years, intervention durations ≥6 weeks for primary analyses, and outcomes including DXA-derived lean mass, one-repetition maximum (1RM) strength, bone mineral density, physical function, and safety. Dual screening, duplicate extraction, and Cochrane RoB 2 assessment were performed. Random-effects meta-analysis used the Paule-Mandel estimator for τ² with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment. Heterogeneity (τ², I²), 95% prediction intervals, subgroup analyses by RT status, exploratory dose/duration meta-regression, small-study effects, and GRADE certainty were assessed.

Results

Seven RCTs (n = 608 randomized; duration 12-104 weeks, median 38 weeks) enrolled postmenopausal women (mean age ≈ 62 y). Lean mass (k = 5; n = 338) favored creatine: mean difference (MD) + 0.37 kg (95% CI + 0.05 to + 0.69; I² = 25%; τ² = 0.01; 95% PI -0.10 to + 0.84). Leg-press 1RM (k = 3; n = 111) improved with creatine: MD + 7.5 kg (95% CI + 2.2 to + 12.8; I² = 0%). Benefits were evident when creatine ≥ 5 g·day⁻¹ was combined with RT; trials using ≤ 3 g·day⁻¹ without RT showed no measurable effect. Bone density was unchanged overall. Adverse events were mild and similar to placebo; renal indices were unchanged. Risk of bias was mostly "some concerns;" one large, preregistered, double-blind RCT was at low risk.

Conclusions

In postmenopausal women, creatine, particularly ≥ 5 g·day⁻¹ with RT, yields small but meaningful gains in lean mass and strength without evidence of harm. Effects on bone density remain unclear.Registration: This review was not prospectively registered. De-identified data and supplementary materials were deposited on OSF after completion of the analysis (DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/BVTRZ).

result.abstractText:
Background

Age-associated sarcopenia and declining physical function in older women are connected to changes in hormones, inflammation, and disrupted protein metabolism. Myokines and cytokines play central roles in muscle atrophy. While both resistance exercise (RE) and essential amino acid (EAA) supplementation are promising interventions, limited randomized trials have assessed their combined effect in healthy elderly populations. Early targeted strategies may help delay sarcopenia and promote healthier aging.

Methods

A 12-week randomized controlled trial was performed involving 96 healthy women aged ≥ 65 years without insulin resistance. Participants were randomized into four groups: control, RE, EAA, or RE + EAA. The intervention consisted of a circuit-based training program conducted three times per week, with each session lasting 60 minutes at moderate intensity. Participants in EAA and RE + EAA groups consumed 5.5g of EAA twice daily. Assessments before and after the intervention included body composition, muscle fitness, serum myokines, and inflammatory cytokines. Data analysis involved two-way repeated measures ANOVA, Bonferroni post-hoc comparisons, and one-way ANOVA for changes in the follistatin/myostatin ratio.

Results

The RE + EAA group demonstrated a significant increase in muscle mass (F(3, 72) = 5.042, p < 0.001, partial η² = 0.174) and greater improvements in the senior fitness test (p ranging from < 0.05 to < 0.001). There was a reduction in myostatin levels (p < 0.05) and an elevation in follistatin in both the RE (p < 0.05) and RE + EAA (p < 0.001) groups. The follistatin/myostatin ratio increased most in the RE + EAA group (F(3, 72) = 5.556, p = 0.002, partial η² = 0.188), with significance versus control (p < 0.001), EAA (p < 0.05) groups. IL-6 and IL-1β were significantly reduced in the RE (p < 0.05) and RE + EAA (p < 0.05) groups, whereas TNF-α decreased only in the RE + EAA group (p < 0.05).

Conclusion

A 12-week intervention combining resistance exercise and essential amino acid supplementation was superior to either intervention alone in enhancing muscle mass, muscle fitness, myokine profiles, and reducing inflammatory markers among healthy older women. These results support the development of early combined interventions for the prevention of sarcopenia and may guide personalized exercise-nutrition prescriptions for optimal aging.

result.abstractText:
Objective

To conduct a comprehensive assessment of physical, functional, emotional, cognitive, nutritional, metabolic, and sexual health in mid-aged women.

Methods

This cross-sectional study was conducted at the Universidad Espíritu Santo Clinic (UEES Clinic), Ecuador, as part of a multidisciplinary integrated health initiative. Women aged 40-60 years were recruited through social media outreach by the UEES Research Center and Clinic between 1 October 2024 and 1 October 2025. Interested participants scheduled a clinical evaluation by telephone. Assessments included laboratory tests (complete blood count, FSH, estradiol, HDL-C, triglycerides, glucose, and thyroid hormones [T3, T4]); validated surveys: Menopause Rating Scale (MRS) for climacteric symptoms and quality of life; Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale, 10-item version (CESD-10) for depressive mood; short Everyday Memory Questionnaire-Revised (EMQ-R) for cognition; and FSFI-6 for sexual function. Participants also underwent anthropometric measurements, body composition analysis, muscle strength testing, and dietary assessment.

Discussion

This methods paper describes a multidisciplinary approach for the comprehensive health evaluation of mid-aged women. It enables early identification of factors affecting quality of life and provides a replicable framework relevant to both local and broader Latin American contexts, serving as a model for similar initiatives across the region.

result.abstractText:
Background

In Sweden 70,000 people suffer fragility fractures annually, including 16,000 hip fractures with one-year mortality of up to 25%. Strategies to prevent falls, improve physical function, and enhance bone strength have shown mixed results.

Aim

To evaluate the incidence of hip and other fragility fractures following a fracture prevention intervention and assess baseline risk factors for long-term fracture outcomes.

Methods

1,233 rural Swedish women aged 70-100 years in 2002 were followed until 2021 after a primary care-based, non-randomized graded fracture prevention intervention 2002-2004 that included physical activity, fall prevention, and pharmacological treatment tailored to hip fracture risk. Fractures were identified through radiology reports 2002-2021.

Results

The most common fractures occurred in the hip with 236 women sustaining 268 hip fractures with highest incidence in women aged 90-94 years. One-year hip fracture mortality was 27%. Hip fractures occurred in 17.7% of the intervention group (77/434) and 19.9% of controls (159/799, p = 0.36). Repeated fragility fractures occurred in 14.1% of the intervention group and 18.6% of controls (OR 0.71; 95% CI 0.53-1.0, p = 0.047), particularly when one fracture involved the hip (OR 0.54 (95% CI 0.31-0.95), p = 0.037). Increasing age (HR 1.8-4.0), height >167 cm (HR 1.6; 95% CI 1.1-2.2), and weight <60 kg (HR 1.5; 95% CI 1.1-2.0) were significant baseline risk factors.

Conclusions

We noticed a non-significant reduction in hip fractures after 20 years, yet repeated fractures were less frequent in the intervention group suggesting a potential long-term benefit. Older, taller and lighter women were at greater risk for hip fracture.

result.abstractText: Postmenopausal oestrogen deficiency is associated with skeletal muscle loss and functional decline, thereby increasing the risk of sarcopenia in women. Considering the safety risks linked to hormone replacement therapy (HRT), alternative strategies are needed to attenuate skeletal muscle decline after menopause. A total of 24 female C57BL/6J mice were randomly assigned to four groups (n = 6 per group): Sham-operated (SHAM), ovariectomized (OVX), OVX treated with estradiol valerate (OVX + E2) and OVX treated with Bazi Bushen (OVX + BZBS). Skeletal muscle mass and function were evaluated in four groups. RNA sequencing was applied to explore the molecular mechanisms and key signalling pathways underlying BZBS-induced muscle protection. We further examined the role of the FGFR1/ERK signalling pathway in mediating the effects of BZBS on myogenic differentiation in C2C12 myoblasts. The results showed that OVX mice had reduced grip strength and skeletal muscle mass, increased fat accumulation, reduced lean mass and impaired metabolic activity. These phenotypic alterations were accompanied by myofiber atrophy, increased collagen staining, endocrine perturbations and elevated expression of p16, p21, Atrogin-1 and MuRF1. BZBS ameliorated these abnormalities. RNA-seq suggested that FGF/MAPK signalling may be involved. In D-gal-treated C2C12 myoblasts, BZBS reduced Atrogin-1 and MuRF1 expression while restoring MYHC and MYOG expression. Mechanistically, BZBS suppressed FGFR1/ERK signalling activation and bFGF partially reversed the protective effects of BZBS. Taken together, these findings suggest that FGFR1/ERK signalling may contribute to the protective effects of BZBS. Our findings provide evidence for the beneficial effects of BZBS on skeletal muscle deterioration associated with oestrogen deficiency.

result.abstractText:
Objectives

This pilot study aimed to: (1) evaluate the effects of high-intensity focused electromagnetic (HIFEM) therapy on pelvic organ prolapse (POP) symptoms and pelvic floor function; (2) compare outcomes across HIFEM, pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) with biofeedback and/or electrostimulation, and usual care; and (3) explore participant acceptability of the interventions.

Materials and methods

A mixed-methods pilot study was conducted in women aged >20 years with stage I-III POP. Participants were randomized to HIFEM, PFMT, or usual care. The HIFEM group underwent twice-weekly 28-min sessions for eight weeks using a non-invasive electromagnetic chair. PFMT consisted of supervised sessions incorporating biofeedback and/or electrostimulation. Usual care included lifestyle advice. Outcomes were assessed using validated questionnaires for POP symptoms and pelvic floor distress, digital palpation, and transperineal ultrasound.

Results

Twenty-eight women completed the study (HIFEM, n = 10; PFMT, n = 9; usual care, n = 9). Compared with usual care, HIFEM significantly improved pelvic floor muscle endurance (p = 0.001), whereas PFMT significantly improved muscle strength (p = 0.034), endurance (p = 0.023), and rapid contractions (p = 0.019). Only HIFEM demonstrated significant improvements in POP symptom severity (p = 0.015) and pelvic floor distress (p = 0.041). No serious adverse events were reported. Participant satisfaction was highest in the HIFEM group (100%). Qualitative analysis supported intervention acceptability, with participants reporting increased pelvic floor awareness, improved symptom control, and enhanced psychological well-being.

Conclusions

Both HIFEM and PFMT with biofeedback appear to be safe, acceptable, and effective non-surgical treatment options for women with POP. Although no significant differences were observed between the two interventions, these findings should be interpreted with caution because of the small sample size. Larger studies are needed to confirm comparative efficacy and inform clinical implementation.

result.abstractText:
Background and aims

Previous metabolomic studies have implicated mitochondrial energy metabolism, lipid remodeling, and carnitine-related pathways in sarcopenia, but broader metabolic pathways linking these abnormalities remain unclear. We aimed to identify sarcopenia-related metabolic pathways by integrating metabolome-wide Mendelian Randomization (MR) with patient-derived serum and skeletal muscle multi-omics analysis.

Methods

Two-sample MR analyses were performed using genome-wide association study summary statistics for 1400 circulating metabolite-related traits and three sarcopenia-related traits, appendicular lean mass (ALM), handgrip strength, and walking speed. Candidate metabolites retained after MR sensitivity filtering were subjected to Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG)-based pathway enrichment. The MR-prioritized pathway was then examined in an independent cohort of 40 postmenopausal women with or without sarcopenia using untargeted serum and skeletal muscle metabolomics. Patient-derived and the external public skeletal muscle transcriptomic datasets were analyzed to evaluate pathway-related transcriptomic patterns.

Results

Lysine degradation was the only pathway meeting the predefined pathway-level FDR criterion in the ALM-negative direction. Lysine, carnitine, and N6,N6,N6-trimethyllysine contributed nominal negative MR associations to this pathway. Colocalization identified strong evidence of a shared causal signal for one carnitine locus (rs1171617; PP.H4 = 0.995). In the validation cohort, nine lysine degradation-related metabolites detected in serum and skeletal muscle were grouped according to three biochemical processes: free lysine oxidation, methyllysine turnover, and trimethyllysine-derived carnitine biosynthesis. In serum, dl-lysine was nominally higher (log2FC = 0.796, P = 0.047) and dl-carnitine was nominally lower (log2FC = -0.130, P = 0.047) in sarcopenia, while the trimethyllysine-derived carnitine biosynthesis score was significantly lower (adjusted P < 0.001). In skeletal muscle, γ-butyrobetaine (log2FC = 1.178, P = 0.029) and N-acetyl-L-2-aminoadipic acid (log2FC = 2.240, P = 0.035) were nominally higher in sarcopenia, whereas none of the three biochemical group scores differed significantly between groups. Patient-derived skeletal muscle transcriptomics were evaluated using predefined Reactome pathways for lysine catabolism and carnitine synthesis; the carnitine synthesis pathway score was lower in sarcopenia (P = 0.049), with significant downregulation of TMLHE (log2FC = -0.411, adjusted P = 0.023) and DLD (log2FC = -0.468, adjusted P = 0.004). In the external skeletal muscle dataset, TMLHE and DLD showed concordant decreases at nominal significance.

Conclusions

Lysine degradation was prioritized as an ALM-related metabolic pathway through exploratory MR-based pathway analysis. Multi-omics characterization indicated heterogeneous and compartment-specific remodeling rather than uniform alteration of the entire pathway, with the most coherent cross-omics pattern involving trimethyllysine-derived carnitine metabolism. These findings support lysine-related metabolism as a candidate metabolic framework for sarcopenia while warranting further mechanistic and longitudinal validation.

result.abstractText:
Objectives

Sarcopenic obesity may worsen during the menopausal transition, but long-term patterns and the influence of physical activity are unclear. We identified sarcopenic obesity trajectories and evaluated their association with physical activity.

Study design

This longitudinal cohort study included 1450 Korean women aged 42-52 years who underwent health examinations between January 2012 and August 2024 and experienced menopause during follow-up.

Main outcome measures

Sarcopenic obesity was defined as skeletal muscle index <5.7 kg/m2 and body fat percentage ≥ 30%, measured by bioelectrical impedance analysis. Group-based trajectory modeling identified sarcopenic obesity patterns relative to the final menstrual period. Physical activity was classified as inactive, somewhat active, or active (<600, 600-2999, or ≥ 3000 metabolic equivalent of task minutes/week). Multinomial logistic regression assessed associations with trajectory membership.

Results

Median follow-up was 10.6 years. Mean annual changes from 11 years before to 9 years after the final menstrual period were 0.215 percentage points in body fat, 0.038 kg/m2 for body mass index, and - 0.011 kg/m2 for skeletal muscle mass index. Three trajectories were identified: stable low-risk (82.6%), peri-menopausal onset (6.0%), and post-menopausal progressive (11.4%). Compared with inactive women, somewhat active women had lower risk of peri-menopausal onset (odds ratio 0.42; 95% confidence interval 0.25-0.71), while active women had lower risk of post-menopausal progression (0.39; 0.20-0.75; P for trend = 0.007).

Conclusion

One-fifth of women experienced adverse sarcopenic obesity trajectories during the menopausal transition. Being somewhat active or active was associated with a lower risk of this, supporting physical activity promotion during this period.

result.abstractText: Postmenopause is characterized by hormonal changes that predispose women to sleep disturbances, alterations in body composition, and an increased risk of sarcopenia. Current studies indicate that weight reduction induced by glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists is associated with decreases in lean body mass, although the functional consequences of these changes, including their implications for muscle and sleep-disordered breathing, are incompletely understood. Importantly, reductions in lean body mass do not necessarily reflect clinically meaningful skeletal muscle loss or impaired muscle function. This narrative mini-review highlights the clinical challenge of balancing effective pharmacologically induced weight loss with the preservation of muscle health and physical function in postmenopausal women. It reviews the current evidence regarding semaglutide use in this population, with a focus on muscle health and sleep-disordered breathing. In this context, overcoming anabolic resistance through adequate intake of protein and micronutrients, and resistance exercise may help preserve musculoskeletal health, although evidence in semaglutide-treated postmenopausal women remains indirect. Although weight reduction is generally expected to improve obesity-related obstructive sleep apnea, the specific effects of semaglutide on sleep-disordered breathing and long-term sleep-related outcomes in postmenopausal women are insufficiently characterized. A more integrated approach to obesity management, combining pharmacological treatment with targeted nutritional and lifestyle strategies, may help achieve safe and sustainable weight loss while preserving muscle function and optimizing overall metabolic health.

result.abstractText: This study aimed to provide a comprehensive oncogeriatric characterization of older women with breast cancer treated in the Chilean public health system and to explore the association between geriatric domains, particularly frailty and nutritional status, treatment decision-making, and early treatment-related toxicity. We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study that included 177 women aged ≥60 years (median age 79 years; range 60-95 years) who underwent a comprehensive geriatric assessment at the Instituto Nacional del Cáncer. Frailty was highly prevalent, with 56% of patients classified as vulnerable or mildly frail (a score on the Clinical Frailty Scale of 4 or 5) and 20.4% as moderately or severely frail (score on the Clinical Frailty Scale of 6-9). Nutritional vulnerability was also common, with a mean Mini Nutritional Assessment-Short Form score of 11.1, low muscle strength (mean handgrip 14.7 kg), and reduced calf circumference in 75.7% of patients, despite a mean body mass index in the overweight range (28.1 kg/m<sup>2</sup>). Most tumours were early stage and hormone receptor-positive; however, frailty, oncogeriatric cluster classification, and nutritional status were significantly associated with therapeutic intent and early treatment-related toxicity (all p < 0.05). Performance status underestimated multidimensional vulnerability compared with geriatric assessment. Treatment plans were modified following geriatric assessment in 40.1% of the cases. Overall, older women with breast cancer treated in the Chilean public health system exhibit a high burden of multidimensional vulnerability that is significantly associated with oncological decision-making and treatment-related outcomes. Comprehensive geriatric assessment provides clinically relevant information beyond traditional oncological metrics and should be systematically integrated into breast cancer care.

result.abstractText:
Background

Fractures in older adults arise from complex interactions between bone fragility, falls, and comorbid conditions. This study aimed to map the comorbidity environment of osteoporosis (M80/M81) by sex and age, and assess whether osteoporosis is systematically coded at the time of fracture-related hospitalization across fracture types.

Methods

We conducted a nationwide retrospective analysis of Austrian inpatient data collected for insurance claims between 2003 and 2014, including 1,705,684 hospitalized patients aged 50-79 years. Comorbidity network analysis was used to characterize sex- and age-specific diagnoses co-occurring with osteoporosis (ICD-10: osteoporosis with pathological fracture M80 and osteoporosis without pathological fracture M81). In paralell, fracture-centered networks were constructed for major fracture types (S22, S32, S42, S52, S62, S72) to assess whether osteoporosis was systematically coded during fracture related hospitalizations. Sex-specific odds ratios (ORs) were calculated to compare comorbidity associations between males and females across three age groups (50-59, 60-69, 70-79 years).

Results

Across all age groups, females exhibited substantially broader M81-associated comorbidity networks than males, with the number of linked diagnoses increasing from 142 to 245 to 330 in females and from 76 to 137 to 164 in males between ages 50-59, 60-69, and 70-79 years, respectively. Fracture-centered analyses showed that across age groups, fractures were embedded within multimorbidity networks rather than forming isolated diagnostic links with osteoporosis. Hip fractures (S72) showed the strongest co-occurrence with osteoporosis diagnoses, particularly in females aged ≥60 years, whereas upper limb fractures - forearm (S52), wrist and hand (S62), and humerus (S42) - showed no osteoporosis diagnoses among significant co-diagnoses in any age group despite these fractures being considered early fragility fractures. In patients aged 50-69 years, male fracture networks showed stronger co-occurrence with trauma-related and alcohol-related diagnoses, while in older age groups networks in both sexes increasingly included neurodegenerative, cardiovascular, respiratory, and renal diseases. In sex-stratified analyses, the co-occurrence between osteoporosis without pathological fracture (M81) and osteoporosis with pathological fracture (M80) was consistently stronger in males than in females across all ages (e.g. OR 63.74 vs 18.53 at 50-59 years).

Conclusions

Osteoporosis is not systematically coded across all fracture types in routine hospital data. Upper limb and thoracic fractures were rarely recorded alongside osteoporosis diagnoses despite being recognized as potential fragility fractures. These patterns suggest under-recognition of osteoporosis at the time of fracture, particularly in younger patients and in males.

result.abstractText:
Background

Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) is a common condition affecting elderly women. This study aimed to evaluate whether combining pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) with electromagnetic stimulation (EMS) provides better outcomes than PFMT alone, using objective three-dimensional (3D) ultrasound parameters.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective analysis of 240 elderly women with POP treated between January 2023 and January 2025. Based on the received treatment, patients were grouped to a PFMT group (n = 114) or a PFMT-EMS group (n = 126). All patients underwent a standardized 15 week intervention. We assessed pelvic floor 3D ultrasound parameters, Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification (POP-Q) stage, pelvic floor muscle strength metrics, and symptom scores pre- and post-treatment.

Results

This analysis included 240 patients. The PFMT-EMS group showed significantly greater improvement in key ultrasound parameters, including a smaller levator ani hiatus area on Valsalva (P < 0.001) and reduced bladder neck descent (P < 0.001). This group also achieved better POP-Q stage improvement (P = 0.013), greater enhancement in muscle strength and symptom relief (all P < 0.001), and a higher total effective rate (P = 0.027).

Conclusion

Combining PFMT with EMS produces superior anatomical and functional outcomes in elderly women with POP than PFMT alone.

result.abstractText:
Background and aims

Postmenopausal osteoporosis presents with heterogeneous comorbidities including cardiovascular disease. Objectives of this study were the identification of clusters of osteoporotic patients in relation to the cardiovascular risk, comorbidities, and levels of intact Fibroblast Growth Factor (iFGF23), a key player of the bone-cardiovascular axis.

Materials and methods

This cross-sectional study in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis took place in the Rheumatology Department, University Hospital Clermont-Ferrand, France. Twelve variables representative of comorbidities were selected according to their associations and clinical relevance: age, bone mineral density, flow-mediated dilation, cardiovascular risk (SCORE2/2OP), muscle mass, handgrip, sleep, quality of life, pain and plasma iFGF23. Multiple correspondence analysis followed by hierarchical clustering was used to propose profiles of patients and associations related to iFGF23 and cardiovascular risk.

Results

Three comorbidity clusters were identified in 102 women (69.1 ± 7.7 years old): clusters of older age with worse outcomes, of younger age with better results and an intermediate cluster. iFGF23 is unveiled as a marker of the cardiovascular risk even in patients with normal renal function, with a threshold of 94.14 ng/L, and is significantly associated with age, fat mass, poor handgrip, poor quality of life, pain and impaired sleep.

Conclusions

Comorbidity clusters of post-menopausal osteoporosis based on the severity of health impairment highlight in this exploratory study iFGF23 as a possible biomarker of the cardiovascular risk. We suggest that iFGF23 measurement may complement SCORE2/2OP calculation to better predict the cardiovascular risk of osteoporosis patients. A suggested hypothesis-generating algorithm is proposed and future validation in a larger prospective study is warranted.

result.abstractText: Background/Objectives: Menopause is associated with profound endocrine, metabolic, immune, and microbial changes that may contribute to accelerated biological aging and increased cardiometabolic risk. The gut microbiome represents a potential interface between estrogen biology, host metabolism, inflammation, and systemic organ function. This narrative review examines the role of menopause-associated gut microbiome remodeling in microbiome-mediated metabolic aging, focusing on the estrobolome, microbial metabolites, organ crosstalk, and microbiome-targeted interventions. Methods: Relevant literature was identified through searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science, supplemented by reference-list screening. Human observational and clinical studies, mechanistic investigations, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and relevant guidelines were critically evaluated and synthesized narratively. No formal meta-analysis was performed. Results: Menopause-associated changes in gut microbial composition and function may influence estrogen metabolism through the estrobolome and modify the production of short-chain fatty acids, lipopolysaccharides, trimethylamine N-oxide, and bile acid metabolites. These pathways may contribute to chronic low-grade inflammation, insulin resistance, endothelial dysfunction, dyslipidemia, hepatic metabolic dysfunction, adipose tissue inflammation, adverse changes in body composition, sarcopenia, neuroinflammation, and urogenital microbial instability. Dietary patterns, fermentable fiber, physical activity, probiotics, synbiotics, phytoestrogens, and menopausal hormone therapy may influence components of this network, although the strength of evidence remains variable. Current data do not support the use of microbiome characteristics to select or dose hormone therapy. Conclusions: The gut microbiome may act as a dynamic mediator linking estrogen decline with metabolic and systemic aging after menopause. However, causality, individual variability, and clinical translation remain insufficiently established. Longitudinal studies integrating shotgun metagenomics, metabolomics, hormone measurements, standardized hormone therapy exposure, and clinical outcomes are needed to determine whether microbiome-derived biomarkers can support risk stratification and personalized interventions for healthier aging in postmenopausal women.

result.abstractText: Background and Objectives: External causes of death remain an important contributor to mortality among older adults. This study assessed long-term trends in mortality due to external causes, transport accidents, falls, and suicide among older adults in Poland between 2000 and 2022. Materials and Methods: Nationwide mortality data obtained from Statistics Poland were used to identify all deaths among individuals aged ≥65 years between 2000 and 2022 (n = 6,645,408). Mortality trends were analyzed separately for women and men aged 65-74 years and ≥75 years. Standardized death rates (SDRs) were calculated using the 2012 European Standard Population, and temporal trends were assessed using Joinpoint regression analysis. Results: Mortality due to transport accidents declined significantly in all age and sex groups. Among women aged 65-74 years, SDRs decreased from 46.6 to 28.1 per 100,000 for all external causes, while among men aged 75 years and older mortality due to transport accidents declined from 62.9 to 16.2 per 100,000. Falls became the leading external cause of death among adults aged ≥75 years and, in recent years, among men aged 65-74 years. Although fall-related mortality initially decreased, significant increases were observed among men aged ≥75 years after 2018. Suicide mortality remained substantially higher among men than women throughout the study period and exceeded mortality due to transport accidents among men for more than a decade. During the final years of observation, mortality due to all external causes increased among adults aged ≥75 years. Conclusions: The structure of external-cause mortality among older adults in Poland changed substantially between 2000 and 2022. While transport accident mortality markedly declined, falls emerged as the dominant external cause of death among the oldest-old, and suicide remained an important cause of mortality among older men. These findings support the implementation of targeted injury-prevention and mental health strategies in ageing populations.

result.abstractText: Background/Objective: Urinary incontinence (UI) negatively affects wellbeing. As it is often seen as a normal part of aging, management is frequently delayed or ignored, challenging healthy aging. This study aimed to characterize UI in community-dwelling older women by assessing sociodemographic aspects, symptoms, pelvic floor muscle strength, urinary habits, and perceptions regarding UI. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional study in older women from four communities in Chile. After educational sessions on UI, women voluntarily enrolled. We applied the ICIQ-SF, and pelvic floor muscle strength was evaluated using the Modified Oxford Scale. We also collected information on UI-related topics. Results: Among 32 older women assessed, 40.6% had stress UI, 3.1% had urgency UI, and 56.3% exhibited mixed UI. The mean ICIQ-SF score was 13.75 ± 3.5, corresponding to severe UI, with a mean score of interference on daily life of 6.75 ± 1.92. Older women exhibited low pelvic floor muscle strength (Oxford: 1.97 ± 1.03), a high prevalence of cystocele (84.4%; n = 27), and coexisting fecal incontinence (40.6%; n = 13). An association between UI severity and pelvic floor muscle strength was evaluated (Spearman's ρ = -0.242, n = 32), but the weak inverse correlation was not statistically significant (p = 0.180). Conclusions: Community-dwelling older women with UI exhibited substantial symptom severity accompanied by low pelvic floor muscle strength, pelvic organ prolapse, coexisting fecal incontinence, and potentially modifiable UI-related habits and perceptions. Although these findings derive from an exploratory sample, they highlight opportunities for community-based education, early detection, and pelvic floor health interventions to support healthy aging.

result.abstractText: Background/Objectives: Sacral fractures are clinically important injuries that may be occult at presentation and may occur after both low-energy falls and higher-energy trauma. National emergency department data describing temporal trends, mechanisms, associated fractures, and disposition remain limited. Methods: A retrospective cross-sectional study was performed using the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System from 2003 to 2022. Sacral fracture emergency department visits were identified using diagnosis and body-part codes with narrative confirmation of sacral involvement. National estimates were generated using NEISS survey weights. The primary outcome was population-based ED visits per 100,000 United States population, overall and stratified by sex. Secondary outcomes included mechanism category, injury location, concurrent vertebral or hip fracture, and emergency department disposition. Results: A total of 1747 sacral fracture emergency department visits were identified, representing an estimated 72,215 national visits. Low-energy falls accounted for 67.9% of presentations. Mean age was 61.1 years, and 70.0% of patients were female. Injuries most commonly occurred at home (50.5%). Annual ED visit rate increased from 2003 to 2022, with a steeper rise among females than males. Disposition varied by mechanism. Motor vehicle or transport-related injuries had the highest admission or hospitalization proportion (54.6%), whereas high-energy falls had the highest treated-and-released proportion (62.0%). In survey-aware multinomial regression, increasing age was associated with lower odds of high-energy falls, motor vehicle or transport injuries, and non-fall other injuries compared with low-energy falls. Male sex was associated with motor vehicle or transport mechanism. Conclusions: National emergency department presentations for sacral fractures increased from 2003 to 2022 and were dominated by low-energy falls among older female patients. However, transport-related and higher-energy mechanisms showed distinct demographic and disposition patterns. These findings supported trauma-system awareness, mechanism-informed co-injury screening, and orthopedic or spine referral pathways for sacral fracture presentations.

result.abstractText: Background/Objectives: Sarcopenia is a growing health concern from midlife, but evidence on its biochemical correlates among postmenopausal women younger than 65 years remains limited. This study aimed to estimate sarcopenia prevalence and explore associations with blood biochemical parameters among Korean postmenopausal women aged ≥50 years using the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) 2025 age-specific diagnostic criteria. Methods: We analyzed 2024 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data from 1157 postmenopausal women aged ≥50 years with complete muscle and biochemical measurements. The 13 biochemical parameters were glycated hemoglobin, total cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, triglycerides, hemoglobin, creatinine, aspartate aminotransferase, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, calcium, phosphorus, magnesium, parathyroid hormone, and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D3. Complex sample logistic regression examined each parameter's association with sarcopenia, adjusting for age alone or age, body mass index (BMI), and age at menopause. Results: The weighted prevalence of sarcopenia was 10.5% overall and 9.7% among women aged 50-64 years. Triglycerides were not significantly associated with sarcopenia in the age-adjusted model. However, in the model adjusted for age, BMI, and age at menopause, each 10 mg/dL increase in triglyceride levels was associated with approximately 5.1% higher odds of sarcopenia (aOR = 1.051, 95% CI: 1.020-1.072, p < 0.001). Higher hemoglobin levels were associated with lower odds of sarcopenia in the age-adjusted model (aOR = 0.734, 95% CI: 0.599-0.901, p = 0.003). Both associations remained significant after false discovery rate correction. Conclusions: These findings highlight the importance of muscle health before older age in postmenopausal women. Biochemical parameters may have potential relevance to muscle health assessment, but their clinical utility requires further validation.

Background

Breast cancer remains the most common cancer among women globally and in Indonesia, with a high burden of morbidity and mortality. In Indonesia, mammography is not yet implemented as a national screening program and is not covered by the national health insurance system. Limited access, high costs, and varying levels of knowledge may influence women's acceptance and willingness to pay (WTP) for screening. This study aimed to assess knowledge, acceptance, and WTP for mammography screening among women in Yogyakarta, Indonesia.

Methods

A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted from July to September 2024 among women aged ≥25 years in Yogyakarta. Data were collected using a self-administered online questionnaire distributed via Google Forms. The questionnaire assessed sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge, acceptance, and WTP using the contingent valuation method. A total of 428 valid responses were analyzed using descriptive statistics.

Results

More than half of respondents (58.6%) had low knowledge of mammography screening. However, acceptance of screening was high (93.0%). Willingness to pay varied across payment scenarios, with 60.0% willing to pay out-of-pocket and 87.9% under a co-payment scheme. Interestingly, acceptance decreased to 43.5% when screening was fully funded by the government. The median WTP was IDR 500,000 (USD 32.5), which falls within the acceptable market price range. Key reasons for willingness to pay included early detection and perceived benefits, while high cost and lack of urgency were major barriers.

Conclusion

Despite limited knowledge, acceptance and willingness to pay for mammography screening were relatively high, particularly under a co-payment scheme. These findings highlight the importance of improving public knowledge and designing financially acceptable screening strategies to enhance participation in breast cancer screening programs in Indonesia.

result.abstractText: The menopause transition is associated with substantial changes in body composition, including increased central adiposity and accelerated loss of muscle and bone mass, that heighten midlife women's risk of obesity and its cardiometabolic consequences. Incretin-based therapies, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and the dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide, have emerged as highly effective pharmacotherapies for obesity, and post hoc analyses of pivotal trials suggest that weight-loss efficacy is preserved across reproductive stages, with postmenopausal women achieving reductions in total body weight, waist circumference, and cardiometabolic risk factors comparable to those of premenopausal women. However, the same pharmacologically induced weight loss that drives these benefits raises concern for postmenopausal women, who already experience declines in muscle and bone related to estrogen deficiency that may be exacerbated by weight loss. Current evidence suggests that reductions in lean mass are generally proportional to the magnitude of weight loss but are often accompanied by improved patient-reported physical function. However, lean mass is not synonymous with skeletal muscle function, few trials have assessed muscle strength or objective physical performance as primary outcomes, and findings on bone mineral density and fracture risk remain inconsistent across studies. This review synthesizes current evidence on the use of incretin-based therapies by midlife and postmenopausal women. It specifically addresses weight-loss efficacy, cardiometabolic risk reduction, body composition, and skeletal health, while distinguishing menopause-specific from extrapolated evidence, and indicating the level of evidence supporting clinical considerations for nutrition, exercise, and musculoskeletal monitoring, to guide a menopause-specific approach to incretin-based therapies.

Background

Endocrine therapy for hormone receptor-positive breast cancer is associated with adverse metabolic effects - including increased fat mass, decreased lean muscle mass, and insulin resistance - that may attenuate the efficacy of GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs). This study evaluated GLP-1 RA-associated weight loss outcomes in breast cancer patients receiving concurrent endocrine therapy.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of 269 breast cancer patients at a single academic center receiving concurrent GLP-1 RA and adjuvant endocrine therapy. GLP-1 RA and endocrine therapy data were obtained from electronic medication reconciliation lists and pharmacy dispense reports. Patients were required to have initiated GLP-1 therapy during the study period and to have received concurrent GLP-1 RA and endocrine therapy for at least one year. The primary outcome was percentage weight change from GLP-1 initiation to 12 months (± 2 months). Secondary outcomes included proportions achieving ≥ 5%, ≥ 10%, and ≥ 15% weight loss.

Results

Mean one-year percentage weight loss was - 4.5% (95% CI: -6.0% to - 3.0%; -3.9 kg; 95% CI: -4.96 to - 2.93 kg), significantly below the 10-20% observed in postmenopausal subgroups of GLP-1 randomized trials (all p < 0.001). Only 21.3% achieved ≥ 10% and 10.4% achieved ≥ 15% weight loss. Weight loss differed significantly by GLP-1 agent (p = 0.003); semaglutide (- 5.8%) and tirzepatide (- 4.7%) outperformed dulaglutide (+ 0.1%), which is approved for type 2 diabetes only. Higher baseline weight was associated with greater absolute loss (r = - 0.19, p = 0.002), though percentage weight loss did not differ significantly by baseline BMI category (p = 0.303). PR-negative patients lost more than PR-positive patients (- 8.2% vs. -4.2%; p = 0.021, d = 0.46). Type 2 diabetes was present in 70.6% of patients; T2DM status was not significantly associated with weight loss on t-test (p = 0.288), though patients without T2DM were numerically more likely to achieve ≥ 15% loss (21.5% vs. 5.8%).

Conclusions

GLP-1 RAs produce statistically significant but substantially attenuated weight loss in breast cancer patients on concurrent endocrine therapy. GLP-1 agent selection significantly influences outcomes. Given emerging evidence of oncologic benefit, prospective trials are needed.

Background

Falls in older women are multifactorial events driven by the complex interaction of age-related loss of physiological reserve, frailty, sarcopenia, chronic low-grade inflammation, multimorbidity, and medication exposure. Older women represent a substantial proportion of fall-related injuries and fractures, yet available evidence is highly heterogeneous. Since many studies focus on mixed-sex cohorts, we must differentiate women-specific findings from general geriatric data.

Methods

A structured narrative review was conducted to integrate biological, clinical, and pharmacological evidence on falls in older women, focusing particularly on primary care. The initial literature search covered PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase from January 2000 to March 2025. To ensure the integration of recent high-level evidence, a supplementary search and backward citation tracking were subsequently executed through 31 August 2026, aligning with peer-review recommendations. Women-specific evidence was prioritized over mixed-sex cohorts. Given that the review aims for an interpretive synthesis rather than quantitative effect estimation, a meta-analysis and formal risk-of-bias assessments were omitted.

Discussion

Frailty and sarcopenia are consistently associated with falls and functional decline in older adults. In contrast, inflammaging and metabolic dysregulation are more strongly supported as contributors to frailty, sarcopenia, and functional vulnerability than as independently established causal determinants of falls. Medication-related fall susceptibility may arise through several mechanisms, including sedation, impaired attention and psychomotor function, orthostatic hypotension, bradycardia, electrolyte and glucose disturbances, gait impairment, and adverse skeletal effects. Psychotropic agents, anticholinergic drugs, opioids, selected cardiovascular drugs, and other fall-risk-increasing drugs warrant particular attention in patients with reduced physiological reserve. Medication review and appropriate deprescribing should be considered components of multidomain fall-prevention strategies rather than stand-alone interventions.

Conclusions

The principal contribution of this review is not the identification of new individual fall-risk factors, but the integration of established biological vulnerability, functional impairment, and pharmacological burden within a sex-sensitive primary-care framework. This approach may help clinicians consider frailty, medication exposure, and women-specific modifiers simultaneously during fall-risk assessment. The proposed framework is hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as a prospectively validated mechanistic or prediction model.

Sarcopenia was diagnosed as per the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) criteria. Sarcopenic obesity was defined as the presence of low muscle mass (relative appendicular skeletal mass-RASM < 5.4 kg/m2) and increased total fat mass% > 40%.

Results

The mean (SD) age and body mass index of the participants were 61.9 (6.8) years and 25.3 (4.8) kg/m2, respectively. Sarcopenia and sarcopenic obesity were identified in 43.7% and 27% of participants, respectively, while 48% had osteoporosis at any site. Although fat mass percentage was lower in those with sarcopenia, multivariable analysis adjusted for age, body mass index, and bone density identified higher fat mass percentage (aOR 1.715, p < 0.001) and lower body mass index (aOR 0.279, p < 0.001) as independent predictors. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis demonstrated good discrimination for body mass index (AUC 0.894) and modest discrimination for fat mass percentage (AUC 0.652); a combined model using body mass index and fat mass percentage improved prediction substantially (AUC 0.946). For sarcopenic obesity, lower body mass index (aOR 0.913, p = 0.010) and higher age (aOR 1.057, p = 0.010) were significant predictors.

Conclusion

Sarcopenia and sarcopenic obesity were prevalent among community-dwelling postmenopausal women, with lower body mass index identified as a significant predictor of both conditions. The observation that low body mass index predicts both sarcopenia and sarcopenic obesity highlights the limitations of body mass index as a measure of adiposity when assessing sarcopenic obesity in postmenopausal women.

result.abstractText:
Background

Osteoporosis and sarcopenia frequently coexist in older adults, yet whether denosumab provides muscle-related benefits beyond bone remains uncertain. We compared denosumab and zoledronic acid across functional, imaging, biologic and study-defined sarcopenia outcomes based on an Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) 2025-informed framework and examined whether early osteoprotegerin (OPG)/soluble receptor activator of nuclear factor-kappa B ligand (sRANKL) responses tracked with later benefit.

Methods

This prospective observational cohort study included 186 postmenopausal women with osteoporosis and prescreened sarcopenia risk (82 denosumab, 104 zoledronic acid). Assessments at baseline and 12, 24 and 36 months included grip strength, gait speed, 5-times chair stand, lumbar spine and femoral neck bone mineral density (BMD), dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)-derived appendicular skeletal muscle mass index (ASMI), computed tomography (CT)-derived T12-L4 skeletal muscle volume index (SMVI), skeletal muscle density (SMD), intermuscular fat volume index (IMFI), visceral fat volume index (VFI) and OPG/sRANKL-centred biologic markers. Continuous outcomes were analysed using linear mixed-effects models, categorical outcomes with Fisher exact tests and responder and mediation analyses.

Results

Denosumab showed greater functional improvement than zoledronic acid. At 12 months, grip strength increased by 1.45 ± 0.51 versus 0.66 ± 0.34 kg, gait speed by 0.041 ± 0.013 versus 0.017 ± 0.011 m/s and 5-times chair stand time by -0.82 ± 0.27 versus -0.32 ± 0.18 s (all p < 0.001). At 36 months, changes were 2.52 ± 0.63 versus 0.99 ± 0.45 kg, 0.070 ± 0.017 versus 0.027 ± 0.012 m/s and -1.47 s (-1.63, -1.34) versus -0.63 s (-0.82, -0.50) (all p < 0.001). ASMI did not differ at 12 months (p = 0.119) but favoured denosumab at 24 and 36 months (both p < 0.001; 36-month change, 0.192 ± 0.059 vs. 0.089 ± 0.050 kg/m2). Sarcopenia prevalence was lower with denosumab at 12, 24 and 36 months (52.1% vs. 69.8%, 30.2% vs. 50.7% and 20.0% vs. 46.0%), and remission was higher (36.7% vs. 15.5%, 63.5% vs. 37.3% and 75.0% vs. 37.0%). Denosumab also produced greater increases in SMVI and SMD and greater reductions in IMFI and VFI. The OPG/sRANKL ratio increased more strongly at 12 months (2.503 [2.053, 3.429] vs. 0.807 [0.549, 0.994], p < 0.001). High responders had larger 36-month gains in grip strength (2.80 ± 0.65 vs. 2.21 ± 0.44 kg, p < 0.001) and CT-defined SMVI (2.816 ± 0.861 vs. 2.199 ± 0.524, p = 0.002). Twelve-month OPG/sRANKL change showed a pattern statistically consistent with partial mediation of the association between treatment group and 36-month grip strength (37.0%) and CT-defined SMVI (39.9%).

Conclusions

Compared with zoledronic acid, denosumab was associated with stronger early OPG/sRANKL activation, earlier functional improvement, more favourable CT-defined remodelling, later DXA-derived muscle-mass gain and lower study-defined sarcopenia burden based on an AWGS 2025-informed framework over 3 years. These findings support validation of RANKL inhibition in osteosarcopenic phenotypes.

Background

Quadriceps weakness, inflammation, and reduced physical function are common in knee osteoarthritis (OA), and lower limb exercise therapy is an established non-pharmacological treatment. Vitamin D3 (vit D3) and vitamin E (vit E) have been proposed as adjunctive therapies; however, clinical findings are inconsistent. We aimed to examine whether combining lower limb home exercises with oral active vit D3 or vit E supplementation provides additive benefits compared with home exercise alone in women with symptomatic knee OA.

Methods

Eighty-eight postmenopausal women with knee OA (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 2-4; 71.9 ± 5.6 years) were randomly assigned to receive therapeutic lower limb home exercise only, home exercise with active vit D3 administration, or home exercise with vit E administration. Participants performed isometric lower limb exercises twice daily for 24 weeks. Subsequently, they were assessed using the Japanese knee osteoarthritis measure (JKOM) as the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes were short-form health survey, grip strength, quadriceps muscle strength, 10-m walk test, inflammatory markers, bone mineral density, and body composition. For data analyses, we used paired and independent t tests, analysis of variance, and analysis of covariance, adjusting for age, body mass index, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade.

Results

Eighty participants completed follow-up. All groups showed significant improvements in JKOM score, quadriceps muscle strength, and 10-m walk test. Grip strength improved significantly only in the group that received active vit D. No significant between-group differences were observed in JKOM scores, short-form health survey-36, muscle strength, or physical performance. Inflammatory markers decreased significantly in the vit E group, although between-group differences were not observed. No other significant between-group differences were found, except in bone mineral density.

Conclusions

Administering active vit D3 or vit E for 24 weeks as an adjunct to lower limb home exercises did not yield significant additive effects on symptoms, muscle strength, or physical performance in women with knee OA. Exercise therapy alone remained effective, and vitamin supplementation showed nutrient-specific trends.

result.abstractText: Background/Objectives: Community-based activities supporting physical function and mental well-being are increasingly relevant in later life. This cross-sectional study compared mental well-being and physical outcomes among older women participating in senior dance only, senior dance plus additional regular physical activity, and physically inactive older groups; a younger inactive group provided exploratory age-related context. A secondary aim was to examine correlations with participation duration. Methods: Participants were 160 women: 66 in senior dance only (SD), 34 in senior dance plus additional regular physical activity (SD+PA), 30 physically inactive older women, and 30 physically inactive younger women aged 25-40 years. Mental well-being was assessed with the Hungarian four-response five-item Well-Being Index (WBI-5), together with seven physical outcomes. Welch's ANOVA and prespecified Welch-Satterthwaite contrasts with Benjamini-Hochberg correction were used; duration analyses used partial Spearman correlations adjusted for weekly attendance and age. Results: Overall group differences were observed for all outcomes (all p ≤ 0.002). Seven outcomes remained significant in Contrast 1, which did not isolate a dance-specific association. No SD versus SD+PA difference remained significant after correction. Within SD, participation duration correlated with more favorable Timed Up and Go (rs = -0.428), 30-Second Chair Stand (rs = 0.425), and 2-Minute Step Test performance (rs = 0.423; all q = 0.0013). The adjusted WBI-5 correlation did not remain significant after FDR correction (rs = 0.271; q = 0.061). Conclusions: Participation duration was most consistently correlated with integrated functional performance. Prospective studies are required; causal effects cannot be inferred. Purpose

This study aimed to examine the associations among sarcopenia, lower urinary tract symptoms, and anxiety in urinary incontinence in community-dwelling older women.

Methods

We analyzed data from 194 older women (mean age: 74.7 ± 5.8 years) who participated in a community cohort study. Sarcopenia was defined according to the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia 2019 criteria. Lower urinary tract symptoms were classified into two groups based on the presence or absence of urinary incontinence, increased daytime frequency, and nocturia. Anxiety was classified into two groups based on the presence or absence of urinary incontinence-related anxiety in urinary incontinence. Associations among sarcopenia, lower urinary tract symptoms, and anxiety in urinary incontinence were examined using binary logistic regression analysis.

Results

Of the participants, 31 (16%) were classified as having sarcopenia, of whom 67.7% had nocturia, which was a significantly higher proportion (42.9%) than that in those without sarcopenia (p = 0.011). Multivariate analysis revealed that sarcopenia was significantly associated with nocturia (odds ratio: 2.61; 95% confidence interval: 1.05-6.49). No association was observed between sarcopenia and urinary incontinence, increased daytime frequency, or anxiety in urinary incontinence.

Conclusions

Sarcopenia was independently associated with nocturia in community-dwelling older women, regardless of the presence or absence of concomitant lower urinary tract symptoms. These findings suggest that sarcopenia is related to nocturia and highlight the potential importance of evaluating sarcopenia in addition to pelvic floor muscles in older women.

Background

Evidence on digital engagement and physical function in rural older adults remains limited. We examined associations between smartphone or tablet ownership, including the diversity of their usage, and physical function among rural community-dwelling older adults.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 248 men and 359 women aged ≥65 years and residing in Japanese rural towns in 2025. Data on smartphone or tablet ownership and usage diversity (e.g., voice calls, LINE, email, Internet, electronic payments, and applications) were collected via a questionnaire. Physical function was objectively measured using handgrip strength, skeletal muscle index, and gait speed. Multiple regression and logistic regression models were used to calculate unstandardized coefficients (B) and odds ratios (ORs).

Results

Smartphone or tablet ownership was reported by 81.9% of men and 82.2% of women. Ownership was significantly associated with higher gait speed in men (B = 0.09, 95% CI: 0.02, 0.17) and women (B = 0.12, 95% CI: 0.06, 0.18). Usage diversity was positively associated with grip strength in men (B = 0.54, 95% CI: 0.06, 1.02), gait speed in men (B = 0.02, 95% CI: 0.01, 0.04) and women (B = 0.03, 95% CI: 0.01, 0.05); conversely, it was inversely associated with sarcopenia in men (OR = 0.59, 95% CI: 0.37, 0.95).

Conclusions

Smartphone or tablet ownership and more diverse usage may contribute to the maintenance of physical function in older adults living in rural areas. Thus, digital engagement could serve as a practical means of supporting physical function in rural settings, where structural barriers can restrict opportunities to connect with others and obtain health information.

Objectives

Sarcopenia is associated with an increased risk of frailty, falls, and mortality. Women exhibit distinct characteristics in appendicular lean mass and metabolism compared with men, and hormonal changes may further accelerate appendicular lean mass. This study aimed to identify key blood biomarkers associated with appendicular lean muscle mass index adjusted by body mass index (ALMBMI) in women and to explore their potential relationship with chronic inflammation.

Methods

Based on NHANES 2015-2018 data from middle-aged women, the ALMBMI was calculated. A multimodal machine learning framework was constructed using elastic net logistic regression and generalized linear models (GLMs) to screen core variables affecting ALMBMI. Weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression and Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR) jointly determined variable weights and effect directions, and restricted cubic spline (RCS) models characterized dose-response curves to identify key blood indicators and their magnitudes of change associated with low appendicular lean mass risk.

Results

A total of 1,082 participants were included in this study. Following variable screening, 12 variables were identified as significantly associated with ALMBMI. WQS regression indicated that segmented neutrophil count (weight: 0.25) and alkaline phosphatase (ALP) (weight: 0.22) were the predominant factors associated with low ALMBMI. BKMR analysis, which assesses all variables jointly, identified segmented neutrophil count (36.0%), and ALP (27.6%) as the core variables. RCS analysis revealed that segmented neutrophil count and alkaline phosphatase showed an L-shaped trend with ALMBMI, with inflection points at 4.00 (1000 cells/μL) and 76.00 IU/L, respectively. In each case, the curves plateaued to the right of the inflection point. Relative to participants classified as having low ALMBMI according to FNIH criteria, those with normal ALMBMI exhibited reductions of 16.01% in ALP and 11.17% in segmented neutrophil count, respectively.

Conclusion

Among middle-aged women, higher segmented neutrophil count and ALP levels were identified as positive correlates of low ALMBMI, with both biomarkers demonstrating threshold phenomena. Such hematological alterations are consistent with chronic low-grade inflammation, underscoring their potential utility in early sarcopenia screening and prevention.

Background

The Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) updated its diagnostic guideline in 2025 to incorporate body mass index (BMI)-adjusted cut-off values for muscle mass and extended diagnostic criteria to middle-aged adults (50-64 years). Using nationally representative data from the 2024 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES), we examined how the new AWGS 2025 criteria influence the prevalence of sarcopenia among Korean adults and characterized age- and sex-specific patterns.

Methods

The study population comprised 2,366 adults aged ≥ 50 years (876 men and 1,490 women) who participated in the 2024 KNHANES. Participants were stratified by sex and age group (50-64 years and ≥ 65 years). Low muscle mass was assessed using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) and bioimpedance analysis (BIA) according to AWGS 2025 criteria, which incorporate both height-adjusted (kg/m²) and BMI-adjusted (kg/m² per BMI) thresholds. Prevalence estimates were weighted to account for the complex sampling design.

Results

Among adults ≥ 80 years, sarcopenia prevalence increased sharply (35.4% in women and 28.8% in men by DEXA). Age-specific prevalence was low in the 50-54 year group (men 2.7%, women 3.2%), rose gradually through the seventies, and increased steeply thereafter. Women exhibited higher prevalence than men in the oldest age group. Comparison between BIA and DEXA measurements showed divergence with age: at 50-54 years, BIA yielded higher appendicular skeletal muscle mass than DEXA (23.77 kg vs. 23.10 kg); at ≥ 80 years, BIA yielded lower values (18.65 kg vs. 20.35 kg).

Conclusion

Application of the AWGS 2025 BMI-adjusted criteria identifies a substantial proportion of Korean older adults at risk of sarcopenia, with women aged ≥ 80 years particularly vulnerable. The divergence between BIA and DEXA measurements in very old adults suggests that measurement modality should be carefully considered in clinical practice. These findings provide timely evidence for public health planning as Korea enters a super-aged society.

Background

Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used for sarcopenia screening, but its added value over conventional models remains uncertain when datasets are moderately sized and predictors are few. We compared logistic regression (LR) with five ML algorithms in older women.

Methods

We analyzed 433 community-dwelling women aged ≥65 years. Sarcopenia was defined as handgrip strength <18 kg and bioelectrical impedance-derived appendicular skeletal muscle mass index <5.7 kg/m2. LR, XGBoost, random forest, a CART decision tree, support vector machine (SVM), and multilayer perceptron (MLP) were evaluated using stratified five-fold cross-validation and pooled out-of-fold predictions. Analyses included a full nine-predictor set and a previously identified set comprising age, height, and calf circumference. A sensitivity analysis used nested cross-validation for hyperparameter selection.

Results

Mean age was 76.2 ± 7.0 years, and 105 women (24.2%) had sarcopenia. In the primary nine-predictor analysis, LR and XGBoost achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) of 0.845 and 0.838, respectively, followed by random forest at 0.832. SVM, CART, and MLP showed lower discrimination. The three-predictor LR model achieved an AUROC of 0.852. With nested tuning, full-model AUROCs were numerically similar for LR (0.835), SVM (0.843), and MLP (0.840); corresponding three-predictor AUROCs were 0.865, 0.850, and 0.852.

Conclusion

LR remained competitive with the evaluated ML models, and the previously identified three-predictor model showed good discrimination. Relative performance depended on model configuration and training procedures. Independent external validation is required before clinical implementation.

Aim

Investigating the effectiveness of 12-week concurrent training associated with nocturnal melatonin supplementation on biological, anthropometric data, and muscle strength in postmenopausal women (PMW).

Methods

Thirty-eight PMW were randomly allocated to three groups: concurrent training (3 sessions/week) associated with melatonin (CTM, n = 13) or placebo (CTP: n = 13) (3 mg/night), and control group (C, n = 12). Biochemical and hematological biomarkers, body composition, waist (WC) and hip (HC) circumferences, as well as muscle strength (one-repetition maximum (1RM)) were assessed pre(T0)- and post(T1)-intervention.

Results

Alanine aminotransferase (p < 0.01), creatine kinase (CK), alkaline phosphatase, glucose, total cholesterol (p < 0.05), aspartate aminotransferase, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) (p < 0.01) decreased while high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (p < 0.01) increased in CTM group compared with C group at T1 and over time only in CTM group (all: p ≤ 0.001 except glucose, total cholesterol: p < 0.01, LDL-C: p < 0.05). Comparatively with CTP, triglycerides (p < 0.05) and HDL-C (p < 0.01) decreased in CTM group at T1. In CTP group, CK (p < 0.05) decreased and phosphorus (p < 0.001) increased over time. Only in CTM group, leukocytes and urea (p < 0.05) decreased while mineral salts (all: p ≤ 0.01 except phosphorus: p < 0.001) increased over time. Fat mass, WC and HC decreased, while muscle mass (MM) increased over time in CTM (all: p < 0.001) and CTP (all: p ≤ 0.001 except WC: p < 0.01 and MM: p < 0.05) groups. Bench press and leg extension (1RM) increased from T0 to T1 in the CTM and CTP groups (p < 0.001), with higher values than the C group at T1 (p < 0.001).

Conclusion

Concurrent training associated with melatonin supplementation was beneficial for metabolic profile, cellular damage, selected renal and inflammatory biomarkers, mineral salts, anthropometric status, and muscle strength in PMW. This combined intervention was also more effective than training alone in improving lipid profile (LDL-C and triglycerides). Training alone had benefits on anthropometric data, CK and phosphorus levels, and muscle strength.

Objective

The purpose of this study was to observe the relationship between sarcopenic obesity (SO) and urinary incontinence (UI) among adult women in the United States.

Methods

A retrospective study was conducted on United States adult women aged over 20 years. Data were extracted from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2001-2006, and 2011-2018 cycles. UI diagnosis was collected via self-report questionnaire about kidney conditions. Sarcopenic obesity was defined as appendicular skeletal muscle mass divided by weight less than 23.47 % and percentage of fat mass equal to or greater than 40 %.

Results

The prevalence rates of stress UI, urgency UI, and mixed UI were 39.6 %, 24.4 %, and 15.7 %, respectively. In univariate logistic regression, women with sarcopenic obesity had higher odds of stress UI, urgency UI, and mixed UI compared to the normal group (odds ratio = 2.048, 2.219, and 2.532, P < 0.001). After adjusting for confounders, the odds remained significantly elevated (adjusted odds ratio = 1.485, 1.554, and 1.663, P < 0.001).

Conclusion

The present study demonstrates that sarcopenic obesity was closely associated with an increased odds of UI in United States adult women.

result.abstractText:
Background

Fat-free mass (FFM) loss after metabolic bariatric surgery (MBS) may influence physical function, metabolic health, and quality of life. Whether FFM loss differs by sex and menopausal status and whether it relates to cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) remain unclear.

Objectives

This study aimed to investigate patterns of FFM loss in males, premenopausal females, and postmenopausal females after MBS and to assess relationships between FFM and CRF before and after surgery.

Methods

In this longitudinal cohort study, individuals undergoing primary MBS with ≥18 mo of follow-up were included. Body weight and FFM were measured preoperatively and at intervals ≤72 mo. CRF was assessed using the Åstrand submaximal bicycle test. Changes in total weight loss (%TWL), FFM, and CRF were analyzed using linear mixed models. Associations between FFM and CRF were analyzed using Kendall's τ and linear mixed models.

Results

The study included 1022 individuals: 221 males, 614 premenopausal females, and 187 postmenopausal females. Males exhibited the greatest absolute FFM loss, whereas premenopausal females lost the lowest proportion relative to TWL (%FFM/WL). At 24 mo, %FFM/WL was 24.7% in premenopausal females compared with 27.1% in males and 28.7% in postmenopausal females. Despite substantial FFM reductions, maximal oxygen consumption improved significantly in all groups. FFM correlated positively with CRF at baseline and until 24 mo in males and premenopausal females; however, postoperative FFM changes were not independently associated with CRF (β: -0.004; 95% confidence interval: -0.008, 0.001).

Conclusions

FFM loss after MBS differs by sex and menopausal status: males and postmenopausal females lose a greater proportion of FFM relative to TWL than premenopausal females. Nevertheless, CRF improves across all groups, showing postoperative gains in CRF can occur despite FFM reductions. These findings highlight substantial interindividual variability in the composition of weight loss after MBS, which is not fully explained by biological sex, menopausal status, or baseline adiposity. Background and aims

To explore patterns of treatment response to pain neuroscience education combined with physical activity (PNE-PA) and to examine baseline characteristics associated with these patterns in older women with chronic low back pain (CLBP).

Methods

In a community-based quasi-randomized trial, older women with CLBP were analyzed in a PNE-PA program (n = 43) or a biomechanical (BM) comparison group (n = 13). Physical function, physical activity (daily step counts by pedometer), pain intensity, disability, and pain-related psychological outcomes were assessed at baseline and 12 weeks. Between-group effects were examined using rank-based analysis of covariance adjusting for baseline values, age, and body mass index. Within the PNE-PA arm, k-means clustering on changes in 30-s chair-stand performance and pain catastrophizing (PCS) was used to identify response profiles, with baseline characteristics compared across clusters.

Results

Compared with BM, PNE-PA produced larger adjusted improvements in chair-stand repetitions, daily step counts, and PCS scores; no significant between-group differences were observed for other outcomes. Three clusters were identified: minimal responders (n = 15), physical-function responders (n = 18), and psychological responders (n = 10). Physical-function responders showed greater chair-stand gains with lower baseline lower-limb function; psychological responders exhibited larger PCS reductions and lower baseline physical performance, together with higher PCS scores. Cluster separation was modest, and the gap statistic favored a single cluster, indicating descriptive, hypothesis-generating patterns.

Conclusion

Older women with CLBP receiving PNE-PA showed heterogeneous changes in physical function and pain-related cognitions. Lower baseline mobility and higher catastrophizing were associated with larger domain-specific improvements, although these associations may partly reflect regression to the mean. Identifying baseline physical and psychological profiles may inform more targeted group-based programs for older adults with CLBP.

result.abstractText: Dermatomyositis (DM) is a rare idiopathic inflammatory myopathy characterized by symmetric proximal muscle weakness and distinctive cutaneous manifestations. It is frequently associated with underlying malignancies, making recognition of paraneoplastic features crucial. We report the case of a 61-year-old postmenopausal woman who presented with progressive proximal muscle weakness, dysphagia, and characteristic skin lesions over the face, neck, and extremities for 6 months. Thorough evaluation with serology, electromyography, and muscle biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of DM. Further investigation revealed an underlying cervical mass, and biopsy established the diagnosis of non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix (Stage IIB). The patient showed partial improvement with systemic corticosteroids and demonstrated significant clinical recovery in both muscle strength and dysphagia following concurrent chemoradiotherapy. This case highlights the importance of evaluating patients with new-onset DM for occult malignancy and underscores the rare but noteworthy association between DM and cervical carcinoma.

result.abstractText:
Background

Urinary incontinence (UI) is a common geriatric syndrome that adversely affects quality of life. Sarcopenia and sarcopenic obesity (SO) may increase vulnerability to UI through the interplay of muscle weakness and excess adiposity, yet their contribution in older women is not well established. This study examined the prevalence of UI across women with sarcopenia and SO and explored its associations with other geriatric syndromes.

Methods

In this cross-sectional study, 535 community-dwelling women aged ≥ 60 years attending a geriatrics outpatient clinic underwent comprehensive geriatric assessment. Sarcopenia risk was screened using the SARC-F questionnaire, muscle strength measured by handgrip dynamometry, and muscle mass estimated via bioelectrical impedance analysis. Obesity was defined by BMI, waist circumference, or body fat percentage, and SO was defined as the coexistence of sarcopenia and obesity. Logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of UI.

Results

UI was reported by 49.9% of participants. Women with UI had higher BMI, more frequent falls, greater frailty, depressive symptoms, higher SARC-F scores, and a greater prevalence of SO. Among the three adjustment methods for SMMI, only BMI-adjusted values showed an association with UI. In multivariable logistic regresion models, fall history (aOR 2.05, 1.38-3.02), SARC-F score (aOR 1.12, 1.02-1.22) and BMI-defined SO (aOR 1.80, 1.09-2.96) independently predicted UI.

Conclusions

SO, sarcopenia risk, and fall history are key determinants of UI in older women. Incorporating muscle and adiposity assessment into continence evaluation may support earlier interventions to maintain continence and independence in this population.
